findings.title: possiblePaths unconditionally includes 'ai' — infinite redirect loop when flag is off
findings.description: Line 152 defines `possiblePaths = ["overview", "resume", "messages", "files", "notes", "ai"]` without gating "ai" on the AI_APPLICANT_SUMMARY feature flag. The `/ai` Route (line 276-283) is wrapped in `<FeatureFlipper feature="AI_APPLICANT_SUMMARY">`, so when the flag is off the route does not exist. However, the `redirector()` function (lines 186-192) will still redirect to `${match.url}/ai` whenever `currentViewPath` is `"ai"` (because `possiblePaths.includes("ai")` returns true regardless of flag state), and with no matching Route for `/ai` the Switch falls through to `redirector()` again — creating an infinite redirect loop. The spec (Section 4, paragraph starting 'Add "ai" to the possiblePaths array conditionally') explicitly requires conditional inclusion: `const possiblePaths = ["overview", "resume", "messages", "files", "notes", ...(isAiEnabled ? ["ai"] : [])]` where `isAiEnabled` comes from `useFeatureFlipper()({ feature: Features.AI_APPLICANT_SUMMARY })`. Neither `useFeatureFlipper` nor `Features` is imported and `isAiEnabled` does not exist in this file.
findings.fix: Import `useFeatureFlipper` and `Features` from `@ats/src/components/shared/FeatureFlipper`. Add `const isAiEnabled = useFeatureFlipper()({ feature: Features.AI_APPLICANT_SUMMARY });` at the component top level (before the useEffect). Change line 152 to: `const possiblePaths = ["overview", "resume", "messages", "files", "notes", ...(isAiEnabled ? ["ai"] : [])];`

findings.title: enabled guard uses `> 0` numeric comparison on a value that can be a fabricated 0 fallback — masks the core rule violation in PlatoTab
findings.description: The `enabled` guard on line 44 is `!!aiJobApplicationSummaryId && aiJobApplicationSummaryId > 0`. This guard is designed to prevent a request firing when no real ID exists. However, PlatoTab.tsx line 41 passes `aiJobApplicationSummaryId: (status === 'succeeded' && aiSummary?.id) || 0`. When `status !== 'succeeded'` or `aiSummary?.id` is falsy/absent, the expression evaluates to `0` — a fabricated fallback — and then relies on the `> 0` guard to stop the request. This is the pattern prohibited by Known Failure Pattern #13 ('Never fabricate fallback values for absent data') and by pipeline rule 13 from the inflow-ats CLAUDE.md. The correct fix is in PlatoTab (pass `undefined` instead of `0` when no real ID exists), but the hook's guard implicitly enables and documents this fabricated-0 pattern. The guard `aiJobApplicationSummaryId > 0` is only safe if callers never pass a fabricated 0; the hook interface (typed as `number`, not `number | undefined`) and its guard together invite this anti-pattern. The spec (Section 7 type changes) types the interface parameter as `aiJobApplicationSummaryId: number` with no option for undefined, which creates pressure on callers to supply a fabricated 0.
findings.fix: Change the parameter type to `aiJobApplicationSummaryId: number | undefined` (or `number | null`). Change the `enabled` guard to `enabled: aiJobApplicationSummaryId != null && aiJobApplicationSummaryId > 0`. In PlatoTab.tsx line 41, pass `aiJobApplicationSummaryId: (status === 'succeeded' && aiSummary?.id) ? aiSummary.id : undefined` — eliminating the `|| 0` fallback entirely.
